..
Issued at 317 AM CDT Sun Oct 25 2026

Quiet and seasonably warm remains the name of the game today and to 
begin the new work week, but gradually gives way to more unsettled 
conditions. Especially by late week and into next weekend. 

The current big picture view across CONUS continues to be 
highlighted by surface high pressure and mid-level ridging 
dominating the east and multiple mid-level troughs or cut-off lows 
providing active conditions over the Mountain West and Pacific Coast 
areas. While Central CONUS is the transition between the two 
regimes, the local area remains dominantly under the influence of 
the mid-level ridge and the westward ooze of the large surface high. 
For today, that means yet another rinse and repeat day for the most 
part with temperatures again well above seasonal norms and in the 
upper 70s to low 80s. Winds will be lighter than previous days given 
the position of the surface high, and high level cloud cover will 
continue to drift across the region. The work-week starts out much 
the same, albeit likely a couple degrees cooler as 925-850mb temps 
are expected to come down from around 13 deg C to 11 deg C. By 
Monday, the current mid-level cutoff low over the SW CONUS will have 
begun to drift NE through the Intermountain West and become more of 
an open wave. Model trends continue to push best large scale lift 
and thus precipitation chances W/NW of the area, yielding no 
mentionable PoPs through Monday evening. 

By Tuesday, the aforementioned mid-level open wave will have 
effectively flattened and shunted the mid-level ridge eastward. This 
most readily allows more southwesterly flow across the region. 
Deterministic guidance depicts a shortwave moving through this flow 
and a smattering of QPF. The QPF may be a bit generous as lift is 
concentrated above 700mb and in an environment with lackluster lapse 
rates / no instability and a dry sub-cloud layer. NBM did populate 
with some low (<25 percent) PoPs at times Tuesday, mainly over W/NW 
areas of the CWA, but have left them in place as some light rain 
cannot be completely ruled out. Wednesday sees steeper lapse rates 
and some increasing low-level moisture helping yield some 
instability, but the lack of a lifting mechanism and cap should keep 
the area dry through the day. By Wednesday night, question becomes 
just how far southward a synoptic front is able to progress. 
Near/along that boundary will be the best opportunity for any 
precipitation, and is reflected in 25-50 percent PoPs mainly over 
northern areas of the CWA Wednesday evening/overnight. Thursday 
yields similar questions to Wednesday, with the position of the 
synoptic front looking to dictate where and if any precipitation 
will be see in the area. Prevailing sentiment among ensemble 
guidance keeps best chances primarily over northern half of the 
area. Temperatures at least partially hinge on cloud cover and 
precipitation chances, but prevailing ensemble solutions point to 
ongoing seasonably warm conditions well into the 70s. 

Rounding out the work week and into the weekend, conditions become 
more active, at least primed for precipitation/showers. Modest low-
mid level moisture return is well corroborated, along with a series 
of shortwaves expected to move through the SW mid-level flow. Given 
timing differences in shortwave arrivals, result tends to be 
broad/area-wide 30-60 percent PoPs moving in late Friday and through 
the weekend. Inevitably, it will not rain that entire time, but a 
wait and see as shortwave timing gets resolved in coming days. 
Unfortunately, this also potentially means a soggy Halloween across 
the area. Temperatures likely cool during this time frame as well, 
but uncertainty in shortwave / potential precip timing yields MaxT 
25th/75th temp spreads approaching 7 to 10+ deg F.
